builds.name: Reference: Critical duel
builds.goal: Reference for Xayah: establish a repeatable reference
builds.hypothesis: A ranged attacker who lays feather lines, threatens return-path roots and uses untargetability to survive an enemy commit. Record feather positions and return paths rather than only feather count. R safety and root access decide whether crit DPS lands; bolts need separate feather-interaction checks. Crit attacks and a conditional shield test repeated duel windows.
builds.summary: Crit attacks and a conditional shield test repeated duel windows.
testPlan: Kit question for Xayah: Record feather positions and return paths rather than only feather count. R safety and root access decide whether crit DPS lands; bolts need separate feather-interaction checks.

Start with the early core (Kraken, then Navori if attack-driven recycling works) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Use this as the control for the other three routes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: Crit attacks and a conditional shield test repeated duel windows. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern.

Q evidence: Xayah throws two damaging daggers that also drop Feathers she can recall. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.

Xayah creates a storm of blades for [4] seconds that grants her [35 / 40 / 45 / 50 / 55]% Attack Speed and cause her Attacks to fire a secondary blade that deals [25]% damage.

When the secondary blade hits a champion, she grants herself [30]% Move Speed for [1.5] seconds.

If Rakan is nearby he will also gain the effects of this Ability, except he gains Move Speed when Xayah strikes a target.

Xayah leaps into the air becoming Untargetable and Ghosted for 1.5 seconds before raining down daggers that deal [200 / 300 / 400 + (1) × AD[statFormula=2]] physical damage and leave behind a line of Feathers.

After using an Ability, Xayah's next @f14@ Attacks will deal @f16*100@% damage to all other targets along their path and leave a Feather for @f12@ seconds.

Lover's Leap: Xayah and Rakan can recall together.

builds.name: Recall angle Spellblade
builds.summary: Build a feather line through spaced casts and change the recall angle with W speed.
builds.goal: Build a feather line through spaced casts and change the recall angle with W speed.
builds.hypothesis: Casts enable feather-leaving attacks; W gives attack speed and champion-hit movement. Essence Reaver rewards one attack after a cast, Stormrazor assists repositioning and Navori tests basic spell recovery through real attacks. E needs three feathers crossing the target to root and exposes crit-stat scaling.
testPlan: Required state: Feathers placed on a recorded line, W champion hit and three crossings at recall.
Record feather locations, E hit count and Spellblade packets with stationary versus speed-assisted recall angles.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Attacks cluster feathers at an ineffective angle or movement puts Xayah outside a safe firing position.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Feather piercing attacks do not prove every secondary target gets all on-hit effects.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Essence Reaver, Stormrazor, Navori Flickerblade, Infinity Edge, Lord Dominik's Regards, Berserker's Greaves. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.

builds.name: Featherstorm opening barrage
builds.summary: Test whether post-R enhanced attacks can quickly add feathers for a defensive recall.
builds.goal: Test whether post-R enhanced attacks can quickly add feathers for a defensive recall.
builds.hypothesis: R grants 1.5 seconds untargetability and leaves a feather line; Fiendhunter's ultimate-triggered three attacks can add passive feathers after landing. RFC tests one safer opening attack while W speed supports an E root angle. The crit budget supports E's explicit stat expression.
testPlan: Required state: R cast before attacks, finite feather lifetime and all attacks inside the item window.
Log item window from R cast through landing, attack count and feathers crossing the same target.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: R travel time or peel denies the volley, and spending R offensively loses a defensive escape.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Fiendhunter's enhanced attack damage does not automatically enhance E as an ordinary crit.
Confidence: speculative. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
